questions.title: Meaning of Standard Deviation and Units

parts.text: Explain the difference between variance and standard deviation with respect to their measurement units, and state why standard deviation is generally preferred when interpreting spread.

Six identical notebooks have a mean mass of $240\text{ g}$ and a standard deviation of $0\text{ g}$.
Explain what the standard deviation of $0\text{ g}$ indicates about the individual masses, and calculate the total mass of the 6 notebooks.

questions.title: Variance and Standard Deviation from Supplied Summary Totals

parts.text:
For $n = 5$ measurements, the summary totals are $\sum x = 40$ and $\sum x^2 = 342$.
Calculate the mean and the variance of these measurements.
For the data in Drill 3 with variance $4.4$, calculate the standard deviation correct to 3 significant figures and state why the square root is not taken before completing the variance calculation.

questions.title: Weighted Sum of Squares in Grouped Data

parts.text:
A grouped frequency table has two classes:
- Class $1$: midpoint $x_1 = 5$, frequency $f_1 = 4$
- Class $2$: midpoint $x_2 = 15$, frequency $f_2 = 6$

Calculate $\sum f x^2$, clearly showing which quantity is squared in each term.

Five concert ticket prices have a mean of $18\text{ dollars}$ and a standard deviation of $0\text{ dollars}$.
Explain what this tells you about each ticket price, and determine the total cost of buying four of these tickets.

questions.title: Grouped Table: Estimating Mean and Variance

parts.text:
The table shows the distribution of a variable $x$ for $10$ observations:
$$\begin{array}{|c|c|c|}\hline \text{Class} & \text{Frequency } (f) & \text{Midpoint } (x) \\ \hline 0 \le x < 10 & 2 & 5 \\ 10 \le x < 20 & 5 & 15 \\ 20 \le x < 30 & 3 & 25 \\ \hline \end{array}$$
Calculate $\sum f x$ and state the estimated mean.
Calculate $\sum f x^2$ and find the estimated standard deviation of $x$.

questions.title: Raw Data: Small Integer Sample Variance

parts.text:
Four students take a short test and score $6,\; 8,\; 10,\; 12$.
Calculate the mean score.
Calculate $\sum x^2$, and hence find the variance and standard deviation of the four test scores, giving the standard deviation correct to 3 significant figures.

questions.title: Grouped Task Times: Mean and Standard Deviation

parts.text:
The completion times, $t$ minutes, for $20$ tasks are grouped as follows:
$$\begin{array}{|c|c|}\hline \text{Time } (t \text{ minutes}) & \text{Frequency } (f) \\ \hline 10 \le t < 20 & 4 \\ 20 \le t < 30 & 8 \\ 30 \le t < 50 & 6 \\ 50 \le t < 70 & 2 \\ \hline \end{array}$$
State the midpoints of the four classes and calculate an estimate of the mean completion time.
Calculate $\sum f t^2$, and hence determine an estimate of the standard deviation of the task completion times, giving your answer in minutes correct to 3 significant figures.

A non-negative continuous variable $x$ begins at $0$. Its cumulative frequencies at upper boundaries $10,\; 20,\; 40,\; 70$ are $3,\; 9,\; 15,\; 20$ respectively.
(i) State the class frequency and class midpoint for each interval.
(ii) Calculate $\sum f x$ and determine the estimated mean.
Calculate $\sum f x^2$ and find the estimated standard deviation of $x$, correct to 3 significant figures.

questions.title: Cumulative Journey Times: 30 Observations to Standard Deviation

parts.text:
For $30$ journey times, the cumulative frequencies at travel times of $20,\; 30,\; 50,\; 80$ minutes are $5,\; 14,\; 26,\; 30$ respectively (starting from $0$).
Find the four class frequencies and calculate an estimate of the mean journey time, giving your answer correct to 3 significant figures.
Calculate $\sum f x^2$ and hence estimate the standard deviation of these journey times, keeping full precision in intermediate steps and rounding your final answer to 3 significant figures.

questions.title: Combined Variance and Standard Deviation Across Two Groups

parts.text:
A class consists of two groups of students who took an aptitude test:
- Group $1$: $n_1 = 12$ students, mean $\bar{x}_1 = 20$, standard deviation $\sigma_1 = 3$
- Group $2$: $n_2 = 8$ students, mean $\bar{x}_2 = 25$, standard deviation $\sigma_2 = 4$

Calculate the combined mean $\bar{x}_{\text{comb}}$ of all $20$ students.
Using $\text{Var}(x) = \frac{\sum x^2}{n} - (\bar{x})^2$, calculate $\sum x_1^2$ for Group $1$ and $\sum x_2^2$ for Group $2$, and hence find the combined sum of squares $\sum x_{\text{comb}}^2$.
Calculate the combined variance and the combined standard deviation of all $20$ students, giving the standard deviation correct to 3 significant figures.

questions.title: Comprehensive Production Quality Control: Shift Comparisons, Outliers, and Variance

parts.text:
A manufacturing process produces metal shafts. For a batch of $25$ shafts from Machine $A$, the lengths $x\text{ mm}$ give:
$$\sum (x - 50) = 15.0,\quad \sum (x - 50)^2 = 41.25$$
Calculate the mean and standard deviation of the lengths of the shafts from Machine $A$.

Machine $B$ produces $15$ shafts with lengths summarized by $\bar{x}_B = 50.2\text{ mm}$ and standard deviation $\sigma_B = 0.80\text{ mm}$.
(i) Calculate the combined mean of all $40$ shafts from both machines.
(ii) Calculate the combined sum of squares $\sum x_{\text{comb}}^2$ for all $40$ shafts.

Compare the performance of Machine $A$ and Machine $B$ with respect to:
(i) proximity to the target shaft length of $50.0\text{ mm}$,
(ii) manufacturing consistency and precision,
(iii) explaining why the combined standard deviation of all $40$ shafts exceeds the standard deviation of Machine $B$ alone.
